themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Most of these problems have no answer key. There is no stable number to grade your work against, and the thing being measured often moves while you measure it, so the models start by building a small truth set of their own or admit the number is only an estimate.
themes.evidence: On answer engine optimization all three models build a fixed panel of real buyer questions because model drift can swing results more than a year of work; identity resolution, cross-channel incrementality, B2B buying-group signal, and agentic traffic all open with the same move of manufacturing labeled examples first.

themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the party holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can force them. The blocker is money and politics, inside the company as well as outside, so the models try to make honesty or cooperation pay instead of writing another rule.
themes.evidence: On agentic traffic every model proposes a fast lane with better data or better prices for agents that declare themselves, and Claude warns the window closes once agents carry the demand; the same logic runs through journey orchestration, where channel bonuses reward sending, and the semantic context layer, where teams are paid on different definitions.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what will happen next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email, a spent dollar, or an exported file cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every model answering safe agent execution builds a proxy or gateway that holds the credentials and caps spend, rate, and audience size, because sends and spend have no rollback; consent enforcement answers apply the same idea with a single gate on every path data leaves the building.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, a message, or a dollar leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can watch behavior from outside and estimate whether the rules were followed, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: On downstream consent and deletion all three models call ad platforms and trained models black boxes with no accepted test for removal; the incrementality answers say the platforms control both the treatment and the evidence, and the agent execution answers note vendors expose no staging or undo primitives.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls turn on meaning, context, and what counts as a good outcome, and no rule set captures that fully. So the models shrink human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than trying to remove it.
themes.evidence: On generative content governance all three build a registry of pre-approved claims and limit what the model may say, because whether wording supports a claim is a contextual legal judgment; the semantic layer answers call one true definition of customer the wrong target, and journey orchestration answers say no single metric captures the trade-off.
